comparison_candidates.name: mspack
comparison_candidates.core_idea: Dedicated mass-spectrometry compressor for mzML and mzXML with both lossless and lossy modes and explicit decode support.
comparison_candidates.why_it_matters: It is a direct codec-style baseline rather than a general container baseline, so it is much closer to mzarc on design intent.

comparison_candidates.name: MScompress
comparison_candidates.core_idea: Multi-threaded mzML to MSZ compressor with random-access decode support and configurable lossless or lossy encoding.
comparison_candidates.why_it_matters: It is a modern practical systems baseline with explicit focus on speed, threading, and usable compressed-file access.

comparison_candidates.name: MS-Numpress in mzML
comparison_candidates.core_idea: Array-level compression inside the mzML ecosystem: linear prediction for smooth m/z arrays and logged or integer schemes for intensities.
comparison_candidates.why_it_matters: It is the closest standard-adjacent baseline for testing whether mzarc beats established PSI-compatible spectrum array compression.

comparison_candidates.name: mz5
comparison_candidates.core_idea: Re-encodes the mzML ontology on top of HDF5, uses binary datasets, compression-friendly layout, and delta mass storage.
comparison_candidates.why_it_matters: The published paper reports roughly 54% of mzML size and materially faster linear read and write, so it is a useful open-format systems baseline.

comparison_candidates.name: mzMLb
comparison_candidates.core_idea: Keeps standards-compliant mzML metadata while moving bulk numeric arrays into HDF5 for better speed and storage efficiency.
comparison_candidates.why_it_matters: It is a direct standard-preserving answer to the same problem mzarc is addressing: less storage and faster access without giving up open-format interoperability.

comparison_candidates.name: Aird
comparison_candidates.core_idea: A computation-oriented format designed around higher compression ratio and lower decoding time, with related StackZDPD work on fast spectral encoding.
comparison_candidates.why_it_matters: It is a strong modern comparison point because its stated goals overlap almost exactly with mzarc: practical compression and decode speed for analysis workflows.
